item.title: Gaming Phenomenon ‘Grand Theft Auto’ Goes Live After 13-Year Wait
item.description: After 13 years of waiting, including two delays and several leaks, the first gamers began playing Wednesday the latest instalment of “Grand Theft Auto”, the most expensive — and among the most profitable — video game ever developed. “GTA VI” becomes available on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series consoles at midnight Thursday in each region where it will be available. That meant it launched first in New Zealand (at 1100 GMT on Wednesday), with many players around the world changing their console location settings to the far-eastern country to be among the first to enter the new Vice City. “I’ve been playing GTA for such a long time that the anticipation for this is crazy,” Australian student Riley Fennel told AFP ahead of the launch. Although Rockstar Games, the studio behind GTA, has not yet released advance unit sales figures, specialist firm Sensor Tower estimates they have already surpassed 15 million. That would be more than $1.5 billion in revenue before the game even came out, for a budget estimated at $1 billion to $1.5 billion, which would be unprecedented. According to the British analytics firm Omdia, sales of “GTA VI” could reach $3.2 billion by the end of the year. An organiser fixes a poster of the video game ‘Grand Theft Auto (GTA) VI’ ahead of its launch party in Chennai on November 17, 2026. Photo by R.SATISH BABU / AFP ‘Taylor Swift of games’ “No other concert or box office release has ever generated that much capital. And so that makes it one of the outliers in entertainment,” said Joost van Dreunen, a professor at New York University’s Stern School of Business. “This is the Taylor Swift of video games,” the industry specialist said. Rockstar’s parent company, US publisher Take-Two Interactive, has rolled out a massive marketing campaign to establish the title as a mass cultural product that transcends the boundaries of video games. “The reach of the game is such that it will lead to a downstream effect on engagement on other entertainment services,” such as streaming platforms, said James McWhirter at Omdia. “I’m going to take four days off,” said Dmytro Shkambara, a 27-year-old Ukrainian player living in Berlin, who said he had been planning this first game session “for a very long time”. Like him, many fans have already booked time off to immerse themselves in the fictional state of Leonida, inspired by Florida. The human resources platform Remote said it had seen a 32 percent increase in leave requests around the world for November 19. Touted as bigger, better and more realistic than its predecessors, “GTA VI” follows the adventures of a Bonnie-and-Clyde-style couple trying to survive in the Miami-inspired, crime-ravaged Vice City. Since its beginnings, the series has won players over with its increasingly realistic reconstructions of fictionalised cities and the great freedom of action offered in a highly detailed open world. item.title: Senate urges FG to implement report on death of 37 miners in NSCDC custody
item.description: The Senate has urged the Federal Government to expedite action on the implementation of the recommendations of its investigative committee on the death of 37 young artisanal miners in the custody of Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps (NSCDC), Niger Command. The News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) reports that the resolution followed the consideration of a motion sponsored by Sen. Sani Musa (APC-Niger East) over the death of the miners on Sept. 17 in Minna, Niger. The senate called for appropriate sanctions against the officers found culpable and institutional reforms within NSCDC to prevent a recurrence of the incident. It also resolved to constitute a delegation to pay a condolence visit to the bereaved families. The lawmakers further directed the Committees on Interior, Solid Minerals, Human Rights, Police Affairs and Judiciary to monitor implementation of the investigative committee’s recommendations and report progress to the senate. Presenting the motion, Musa said the deceased were arrested during operations against suspected illegal mining activities but subsequently died under circumstances that raised concerns about their conditions of detention and protection of fundamental human rights. He said that the federal government had established a 10-member independent investigative committee, chaired by Mr Jonathan Kure, to establish the circumstances surrounding the deaths, determine responsibility and recommend appropriate measures. Musa noted that the committee had submitted its report, identifying lapses and recommending sanctions, institutional reforms and financial compensation for the families of the deceased. Seconding the motion, Sen. Ned Nwoko (APC-Delta North) described the incident as a national tragedy but called for an objective examination of the circumstances surrounding the deaths. “It is a national tragedy when so many young lives are lost under circumstances such as the ones we are discussing,” Nwoko said. He, however, observed that similar incidents involving young people allegedly engaged in illegal activities occurred in oil-producing communities in the South-South. “I believe we should apply the same standards when dealing with issues of this nature. A human life is a human life, irrespective of where the incident occurs,” he said. Responding, the Senate President, Godswill Akpabio, said the motion was necessary to bring the incident to national attention and commended the federal government for establishing an investigative panel. Akpabio said the senate should not prejudge the outcome of the investigation but must recognise the circumstances surrounding the deaths. “Under Nigerian law, every person is presumed innocent until proven guilty,” he said. The senate president added that the deceased had not been given the opportunity to defend themselves before a competent court. “They are Nigerians who were not given the opportunity to defend themselves. item.title: State Police: Senate Directs NASS Clerk To Transmit Amendment Bill To Tinubu For Assent
item.description: The Senate has directed the clerk to the National Assembly to transmit the Constitution alteration bill providing for the establishment of State Police to President Bola Tinubu for assent. The upper chamber has also asked the Executive to forward the National Policing Bill to the National Assembly for legislative scrutiny and expeditious passage to establish the operational framework for subnational policing. The resolutions followed a motion sponsored by the Senate Leader, Opeyemi Bamidele, during plenary today. Policemen at the Niger State Police Command (Photo by Abdullahi Egba/Channels TV) In its deliberations, Senator Bamidele recalled that the National Assembly had processed an executive bill seeking to amend the 1999 Constitution to establish state police as part of Nigeria’s national policing structure. He noted that both chambers overwhelmingly approved the proposed amendment, with the Senate passing the bill on June 24, 2026, and the House of Representatives following suit on July 23, 2026, securing the constitutionally required two-thirds majority. The bill was subsequently transmitted to the 36 State Houses of Assembly for approval in line with Section 9(2) of the Constitution. The Senate Leader noted that the Senate confirmed that all 36 state legislatures had now endorsed the proposed amendment and transmitted their resolutions to the National Assembly. Having satisfied the constitutional requirements under Sections 9(1) and 9(2), the Senate maintained that the amendment had fulfilled the conditions necessary for its passage. The upper chamber therefore urged the Executive to submit the National Policing Bill to provide the legal and operational framework for the implementation of State Police. The Clerk to the National Assembly, Kamoru Ogunlana, announced on Monday that all 36 State Houses of Assembly had approved the proposed constitutional amendment to establish state police, clearing the way for the bill to be transmitted to President Bola Tinubu for assent. The clerk described it as 100 per cent approval by the state legislatures, as the approval exceeded the constitutional requirement of at least 24 state assemblies under Section 9(2) of the 1999 Constitution, as amended. “The Clerk to the National Assembly wishes to announce that all the thirty-six (36) State Houses of Assembly have approved ‘A Bill for an Act to Alter the Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, 1999 to Provide for the Establishment of State Police Services and for related Matters’. “This represents one hundred percent (100%) endorsement by the State Houses of Assembly, which exceeds the threshold of twenty-four (24), provided under Section 9(2) of the Constitution (as amended),” Ogunlana had stated. The development marked the completion of the state assemblies’ consideration of the proposed amendment, following weeks of legislative engagement over the establishment of state police. item.title: 2027: My US congressional meetings not for endorsement — Obi
item.description: By Efe Onodjae The presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Peter Obi, has clarified that his recent meetings with members of the United States Congress in Washington, DC, were not intended to secure endorsements for his political ambition. Obi, who made the clarification in a statement posted on his Facebook page, said reports suggesting that his engagements with American lawmakers amounted to endorsements of his political aspirations were inaccurate. He explained that the visit was primarily aimed at engaging congressional leaders and other influential American stakeholders on issues concerning Nigeria’s development, citizens’ welfare and the consolidation of democracy. The post read; “I wish to address the inaccurate interpretation presented in certain media reports concerning my recent engagements with members of the United States Congress in Washington, DC. “As I expressly noted in my remarks, my visit to the United States was not intended to secure an endorsement, and I did not characterise my meetings as endorsements of my political aspirations by the US Congress or any of its members. “The primary purpose of the visit was to engage with congressional leaders and other influential American stakeholders, exchange perspectives, and discuss matters related to Nigeria’s development, the welfare of our citizens and, most importantly, the consolidation of our democracy. “I am especially concerned with strengthening democratic institutions, advancing accountability, and ensuring that Nigeria’s electoral process produces elections that are free, fair, transparent and credible. These matters should concern every Nigerian who is committed to our country’s future. “I consider engagements of this kind valuable, and I encourage other Nigerian political leaders, especially those seeking public office, to pursue similar discussions with international stakeholders. Our democracy can be strengthened through constructive dialogue, the exchange of experiences and a shared commitment to credible elections.“ The post 2027: My US congressional meetings not for endorsement — Obi appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Tinubu’s tough reforms will ensure lasting prosperity for Nigeria – Wike
item.description: Minister of the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), Mr Nyesom Wike, has urged market traders in Abuja to rally behind President Bola Tinubu’s re-election bid in 2027 for lasting prosperity. Wike, who made the call during a town hall with various market associations across the nation’s capital in Abuja on Wednesday, stressed that Tinubu administration’s economic reforms were laying the foundation for long-term national growth and stability. He acknowledged the economic difficulties triggered by the removal of the fuel subsidy but maintained that previous administrations lacked the courage to confront what he described as a systemic scam. “This country is nearly gone. For you to say that you must try to change what is happening means that you must lay a foundation first, and when you lay a foundation, you give it time to grow. “There is no government that has not identified that this oil subsidy is a scam, why university teachers cannot work, no payment of salaries, no payment of pensioners. “Everybody is afraid; they lack courage. If you don’t have good leaders who have courage to take decisions, that country will not grow,” he added. According to the minister, the temporary sacrifices necessitated by the subsidy removal have yielded tangible benefits nationwide. “This includes increased revenue allocations to states and local governments, clearance of pension backlogs, and an end to recurring strikes by the Academic Staff Union of Universities (ASUU).” Wike cautioned Nigerians against politicians promising to reverse the subsidy removal, arguing that such rhetoric was deceptive and would set the country backwards. “If we allow these policies that the government has put in place to mature, what is going to happen in the next four years will be good. Forget about people coming to tell you stories,” he said. Highlighting his administration’s achievements in Abuja since assuming office in August 2023, Wike pointed to ongoing and completed road infrastructure projects in satellite towns and districts, noting that good road networks were critical for reducing transportation costs and boosting commerce. He pledged to grant approval for the further development of markets in the territory and promised to hold regular interactive sessions with traders at least once every six months. Beyond physical infrastructure, the minister underscored institutional reforms approved by Tinubu for the FCT, noting that for the first time since the territory’s creation in 1976, an indigene was appointed to the Federal Executive Council. He also cited the establishment of the FCT Civil Service Commission, which allows career civil servants to rise to the rank of Permanent Secretary and Head of Service, and the creation of Mandate Secretariats for Women and Youth. item.title: ‎CP Azare Charges Newly Promoted Officers On Discipline, Commitment To Duty
item.description: Akwa Ibom State Commissioner of Police, CP Baba Azare, has charged the newly promoted senior officers of the Command to live up to the demands of their new ranks and justify the confidence reposed in them. ‎CP Azare gave the charge when he decorated the officers with their new ranks at the Command headquarters, Ikot Akpanabia, Uyo, on Monday. ‎The newly promoted senior officers were decorated with new ranks following their recent promotion by the Police Service Commission. ‎The Police Commissioner, who congratulated the officers on what he acknowledged as their well-deserved promotions, described their elevation as recognition of their dedication, professionalism, hard work and commitment in the discharge of their duties. ‎“Promotion comes with higher responsibilities and more expectations. You are therefore charged to justify the confidence reposed in you through greater commitment to duty, professionalism, respect for human rights and strict adherence to the rule of law.” CP Azare advised. ‎The promoted senior officers comprise three Chief Superintendents of Police (CSPs) namely: CSP Richard Oguntola, CSP Magret Alapa, CSP Bokima Bassey, three Superintendents of Police (SPs) namely: SP John Mamodu, SP Glory George, SP Victor Lane and two Deputy Superintendents of Police (DSPs) namely: DSP Emmanuel Ayoka and DSP Godwin Awana. ‎CP Azare commended the Police Service Commission for the timely promotion of deserving officers, noting that such a gesture would further boost morale and inspire more commitment among officers. ‎The Commissioner also expressed gratitude to the Inspector-General of Police, IGP Olatunji Rilwan Disu, for his visionary leadership, support and sustained commitment to the welfare of officers of the Nigeria Police Force. ‎CSP Richard Oguntola, responding on behalf of the newly promoted officers, expressed appreciation to the Almighty God for His mercy and grace to witness another memorable achievement. ‎He also expressed gratitude to the Police Service Commission and the Inspector-General of Police for finding them worthy for promotion. ‎CSP Oguntola particularly thanked CP Azare for his exemplary leadership, encouragement and support, which he stated had positively impacted their career progression. ‎He reiterated their commitment to the professional discharge of the constitutional duties of the Nigeria Police Force in their respective areas of responsibility in line with international best practices. ‎The decoration ceremony was attended by members of the management team, officers of the Command, families, friends and well-wishers who joined in celebrating the officers on their well-deserved promotions. ‎ ‎ The post ‎CP Azare Charges Newly Promoted Officers On Discipline, Commitment To Duty appeared first on Channels Television .

item.title: Putin-Trump-Xi: Three men, three different agendas
item.description: An unprecedented trilateral summit of the leaders of China, Russia and the US will provide startling images and unsettle Europe this week, but all three presidents are approaching the meeting with starkly different agendas. Donald Trump, Vladimir Putin and Xi Jinping will meet Thursday on the sidelines of the APEC summit in the Chinese city of Shenzhen for talks that have echoes of the US-UK-USSR February 1945 “big three” summit in Yalta. At that meeting, which took place months before the end of World War II, the leaders of Britain, the Soviet Union and the US agreed the postwar division of Europe. Europe, which will not have a representative at Thursday’s talks, will be eyeing them warily. The smiles and friendly handshakes may also cause chills in Ukraine, after almost half a decade of war with Russia, and Taiwan, the democratic island viewed by China as part of its territory. But analysts say it is unlikely that the meeting will result in a landmark breakthrough on key issues such as Ukraine, nuclear disarmament and AI, even if the fact it is taking place at all is remarkable. Here AFP looks at what the three men will want from the meeting. Putin: imagery and Ukraine On paper, Putin will be in the meeting as the junior partner, presiding over a country whose population, let alone economy, is dwarfed by both the United States and China. But the war sparked by Moscow’s invasion of Ukraine, which Trump famously vowed to resolve in 24 hours, will be at the centre of the talks as the conflict grinds towards its fifth anniversary. Putin will be buoyed by being able to set out his conditions for ending the war without Kyiv’s chief allies, the Europeans, or Ukraine being at the table. “He wants Russia, the US and China to decide everyone else’s geopolitical fate. But in the end it’s impossible to decide on the fundamentals of European security without Europeans,” said Fredrik Wesslau, senior policy fellow at the European Council on Foreign Relations (ECFR). The optics of the meeting, set to be relayed extensively by Russia’s state-controlled media, are also very important for Putin who has always pressed for Moscow to be seen as a great global power even after the collapse of the USSR. “A seat alongside the American and Chinese presidents would affirm Russia’s status as a global power, despite its much weaker economic position,” said Tsiporah Fried, senior fellow at the Hudson Institute. “Political rehabilitation would be a gain even without concessions on territory, sanctions, or Ukraine’s future alignment,” she added. Trump: nuclear and overcoming midterms Trump and the White House have framed the trilateral summit as a way of advancing nuclear arms control, although the president himself admitted before leaving Washington “it’s a tough subject because it’s very hard for any of us to say we’ll get rid of our nukes.” The imagery is also important for Trump as the 80-year-old contemplates his last two years in office as a lame-duck president followin

item.title: Supreme Court reserves judgment in Zamfara North APC senatorial dispute
item.description: By Ikechukwu Nnochiri ABUJA – The Supreme Court on Wednesday reserved judgment in the legal dispute concerning the All Progressives Congress (APC) primary election for the Zamfara North Senatorial District, ahead of the 2027 general elections. A five-member panel of the court, led by Justice Tijani Abubakar, reserved the matter for judgment after the contending parties adopted their respective briefs of argument. The appeal, marked SC/CV/840/2026, was lodged before the apex court by Senator Sahabi Ya’u, who is seeking to set aside a verdict the Sokoto Division of the Court of Appeal delivered in the matter. The APC had declared that Senator Ya’u won a primary election it conducted in the senatorial district on May 19. However, dissatisfied with the outcome of the primary, a governorship aspirant of the party, Dr. Sani Abdullahi Shinkafi, took the matter to court. While challenging the process that led to the emergence of Senator Ya’u as the party’s flag bearer, Shinkafi told the court that no valid primary was conducted in the senatorial district. Processes before the court showed that the party had cleared three aspirants, Hanafi Musa Moriki, Shinkafi and Ya’u, to contest the primary poll. Shinkafi, in his suit, maintained that, contrary to the APC’s position, no valid consensus was reached among the aspirants to warrant the nomination of Senator Ya’u as the unopposed candidate. He told the court that he neither withdrew nor endorsed anyone as a consensus nominee, adding that he did not submit any written consent to withdraw from the race. Cited as respondents in the matter were the APC, INEC and Senator Ya’u. Meanwhile, in a judgment delivered on August 31, Justice Hassan Dikko of the Federal High Court in Gusau, Zamfara State, nullified the primary poll and ordered the APC to conduct a fresh one within 14 days. The high court held that the action of the APC was not in tandem with the principle of internal democracy entrenched in the party’s Constitution. Dissatisfied with the judgment, Senator Ya’u lodged an appeal before the Sokoto Division of the Court of Appeal. He, among other things, challenged the jurisdiction of the high court to meddle in a matter he said was within the realm of the domestic affairs of a political party and therefore non-justiciable. However, the appeal was dismissed, as the appellate court upheld the high court’s decision in the matter. Not happy with the verdict, Senator Ya’u approached the Supreme Court to set aside the concurrent decisions of the two lower courts. While the appellant argued his case on Wednesday through a team of lawyers led by Mr. Wale Balogun, SAN, the 1st respondent, Dr. Shinkafi, was represented by Mr. Bello Galadi, who filed a brief of argument on November 13 urging the court to dismiss the appeal for want of merit. item.title: NLC, TUC end rift, unite against anti-worker policies
item.description: By Victor Ahiuma-Young Nigeria’s two major labour centres, the Nigeria Labour Congress (NLC) and the Trade Union Congress of Nigeria (TUC), have resolved their differences and agreed to strengthen their cooperation following the intervention of former leaders of both organisations. The reconciliation, announced at a joint world press conference on Wednesday, November 18, 2026, marks an end to the public disagreement that had threatened unity within the organised labour movement. The peace deal was brokered by former presidents of the two labour centres, who intervened to resolve the dispute and restore harmonious working relations between their leaderships. In a joint statement signed by NLC President, Comrade Joe Ajaero, and TUC President General, Comrade Festus Osifo, the organisations reaffirmed their commitment to unity, solidarity and the protection of Nigerian workers’ rights and welfare. The statement acknowledged that a misunderstanding between the two labour centres had played out in the public domain but said the intervention of their former leaders had successfully resolved the disagreement. “It is no longer news that a family misunderstanding arose between the two Labour Centers, which unfortunately played out in the public domain. However, in the true spirit of labour solidarity, maturity and collective responsibility, distinguished former presidents of NLC and TUC intervened and worked tirelessly to resolve the disagreements. “We are pleased to announce that their intervention has yielded the desired results, and the misunderstanding has been amicably resolved,” the statement said. The two organisations declared that the unity of Nigerian workers was more important than disagreements among their leaders, pledging to work together in the interest of workers, pensioners and other vulnerable groups. They said the challenges confronting Nigerian workers required solidarity rather than division, adding that their common struggle must not be undermined by institutional differences or leadership disagreements. Both centres also reaffirmed that workers’ welfare, dignity and material well-being remained non-negotiable, stressing that their renewed partnership would focus on confronting exploitation, defending decent work, demanding economic justice and resisting policies they consider detrimental to workers and pensioners. “We are determined to ensure that our differences do not provide an opportunity for anti-worker forces to weaken the labour movement or undermine the gains achieved through decades of collective struggle,” they said. To sustain the reconciliation, the labour centres said they had agreed to introduce measures to promote mutual respect, strengthen working relations, establish effective mechanisms for resolving future disagreements and prevent a recurrence of such disputes. item.title: JAMB ends office visits for course changes
item.description: By Joseph Erunke, Abuja The Joint Admissions and Matriculation Board (JAMB) has introduced a fully online process for candidates seeking to change their preferred institutions or courses, eliminating the need for physical visits to its offices to access the service. The new arrangement allows candidates to independently make the changes through the Board’s e-Facility portal from any location with internet access. The initiative is expected to reduce queues, transportation costs, waiting time and other inconveniences associated with physically accessing the service. In a statement issued by its Acting Director, Public Affairs and Protocol, Dr Fabian Benjamin, the Board said the development was part of efforts to improve service delivery and align its operations with the Federal Government’s Ease of Doing Business policy. Under the arrangement, candidates can complete the entire process, including payment, authentication and submission, online without visiting JAMB offices or accredited facilities. To access the service, candidates are required to log into the JAMB e-Facility portal at https://efacility.jamb.gov.ng using their registered email addresses and passwords. After logging in, they should select “Corrections and Uploads” from the sidebar menu, click on “Change of Programme/Institution”, select UTME and indicate the examination year for which the correction is required. Candidates are then expected to generate a payment invoice by clicking on “Make New Payment” and complete the transaction through the CREDO payment platform using a debit card or bank transfer. The Board advised candidates to return to the payment page on their profiles after making payment to confirm that the status has changed from “PENDING” to “PAID (Not Used)”. After confirming payment, candidates should return to the Change of Institution/Course page, enter their preferred institution and/or programme details and validate the transaction using a One-Time Password (OTP) sent to their registered email addresses. The process is completed by clicking the “SAVE” button, after which a confirmation message indicating that the change has been successfully made will be displayed. Candidates are also required to print their Change of Programme/Institution slips and log into the Central Admissions Processing System (CAPS) to confirm that their new choices have been updated. JAMB cautioned candidates to carefully review their selections before submitting requests to avoid errors. It also stressed that candidates must ensure their payment status reads “PAID (Not Used)” before proceeding and have access to their registered email accounts to receive and validate the OTP. The Board further advised candidates to carry out the process through their individual profiles rather than engage intermediaries or disclose their login details and OTPs to third parties. item.title: US Congress neither met nor endorsed Obi – Atiku’s lobbyists
item.description: A Washington-based lobbying firm hired by former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar, Von Batten-Montague-York, has dismissed reports that the United States Congress met with or endorsed the presidential ambition of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) candidate, Peter Obi. The firm said the event attended by Obi during his visit to Washington, DC, was a private gathering and did not constitute an official meeting with the US Congress. The clarification followed reports suggesting that Obi had secured the endorsement of members of the US Congress for his 2027 presidential ambition. Obi had announced on his X platform that he arrived in Washington, DC, on Monday, November 16, for a series of meetings and engagements with congressional leaders from both the House of Representatives and the Senate, as well as other influential American figures. He said the discussions focused on Nigeria’s development, security, economic prosperity and the future of the country’s democracy. However, Von Batten-Montague-York, in a statement posted on its X platform on Tuesday, said neither the Congress nor its relevant foreign affairs committee met with or endorsed Obi. The firm’s principal, Dr Von Batten, said he was responding to media reports claiming that Obi had received congressional endorsement, particularly after his firm was mentioned in a public commentary. He said, “Congress did not meet with or endorse Mr. Obi. The event he attended was private, and no one in the video is a member of the House Foreign Affairs Committee or its Subcommittee on Africa, which oversees U.S. foreign policy toward Africa. “I know everyone in the video, and no official from the State Department’s Bureau of African Affairs appears in it either.” Batten said he recognised Congressman Marlin Stutzman and Congresswoman Beth Van Duyne, who were among the American figures Obi identified as having met during his visit. He, however, noted that neither lawmaker served on the House Foreign Affairs Committee, adding that they served on committees responsible for budget and small business matters. He said his clarification was not intended to diminish the significance of Obi’s visit but to correct what he described as inaccurate reports. In his earlier account of the visit, Obi said he held a substantive interview with American television commentator Glenn Beck, during which they discussed Nigeria’s challenges, accountable leadership and the management of the country’s resources. He also listed Stutzman, Van Duyne, former Congressman Todd Tiahrt, Suzanne Bock Grisham and retired US Army Colonel Albert V. Short among the people he met. Obi further said he addressed an audience on Capitol Hill, where he highlighted the need for international cooperation and support for Nigeria, particularly in security, national unity, economic development and democratic governance. item.title: Army intercepts 300 rounds of ammunition concealed in beans sack
item.description: By Kingsley Omonobi ABUJA — Troops of the Nigerian Army have arrested a 47-year-old man suspected of transporting ammunition to individuals in Kogi State, recovering 300 rounds of 7.62mm by 39mm ammunition concealed in a sack of beans. The interception followed an intelligence-led operation aimed at disrupting the supply of weapons and ammunition to criminal groups. The Army said the suspect, identified as Umaru Muhammad, a resident of Ashe Village, was intercepted at about 9:30pm on Tuesday, November 17, 2026, by troops of the Atsawa Blocking Force working with local vigilantes. In a statement on Wednesday, the Acting Director, Army Public Relations, Colonel Appolonia Anele, said a search of the suspect’s belongings led to the discovery of the ammunition concealed in the sack of beans. According to the statement, preliminary interrogation indicated that the ammunition was allegedly intended for two individuals identified as Gimba and Dare, reportedly residents of Gori Village along the River Niger corridor in Lokoja Local Government Area of Kogi State. The Army said the identities and alleged roles of the individuals were being investigated, adding that the circumstances surrounding the attempted transfer of the ammunition remained subject to further inquiries. Other items recovered from the suspect included a Bajaj motorcycle, a mobile telephone and ₦30,500 in cash. Muhammad is currently in military custody as investigations continue to establish the circumstances surrounding the alleged ammunition transaction and identify other persons who may be connected to it. The Army said the operation formed part of its ongoing efforts to disrupt the supply of arms, ammunition and other logistics to groups involved in terrorism, banditry and kidnapping. It added that troops would sustain intelligence-driven operations and strengthen cooperation with local security stakeholders to prevent criminal activities. The Army also urged members of the public to report suspicious movements, particularly the transportation of concealed arms, ammunition and other prohibited items, to security agencies. It reaffirmed its commitment to protecting communities and supporting efforts to restore peace and security across the country. item.title: Arewa group faults northern elders over Tinubu criticism
item.description: … Calls for broader consultation before claiming to speak for North By Ibrahim Hassan-Wuyo KADUNA — The Arewa Emerging Elites Round Table has disagreed with recent comments by Dr Hakeem Baba-Ahmed, Dr Usman Bugaje, former Minister Adamu Maina Waziri and Prof Usman Yusuf on President Bola Tinubu’s administration, insisting that the views of a few individuals should not be presented as the collective position of Northern Nigeria. The group made its position known at a press conference in Kaduna, where it called for broader consultation among stakeholders before anyone claims to speak on behalf of the region. Reading a briefing titled, “Stop Hiding Naked Partisanship Behind the Sacred Robes of Arewa Eldership: You Do Not Speak for the North!”, the group’s chairman, Abubakar A. Kurawa, said Northern Nigeria comprised diverse interests and perspectives that should be adequately represented in public discussions. The organisation expressed concern over what it described as attempts to interpret comments made at a book presentation in Abuja as reflecting the position of the 19 Northern states. It questioned whether traditional rulers, religious leaders, youth organisations, professional groups and ordinary citizens across the region had been adequately consulted before such positions were presented as representing the North. The group maintained that individuals had the constitutional right to criticise government policies and express concerns about the administration but argued that such opinions should be clearly distinguished from the collective position of the region. It said public discussions about the performance of the Federal Government should accommodate different perspectives rather than suggest that a particular gathering or group of individuals represented the views of all Northern Nigerians. The Round Table also called on political leaders and former public office holders from the region to demonstrate accountability by highlighting their contributions to the development of Northern Nigeria. It stressed that discussions about leadership and governance should focus on measurable contributions to addressing the challenges confronting the region. The organisation further urged Northern stakeholders to give greater attention to insecurity, agriculture, infrastructure, education and economic development, describing them as critical issues requiring sustained engagement with governments at all levels. It said political and developmental interests of the North should take precedence over individual political interests and called for constructive engagement with the Federal Government on issues affecting the region. The group also emphasised that criticism of government policies remained an important feature of democratic governance, adding that public officials should be open to scrutiny and accountability. item.title: Plateau killings: Obi condemns attacks, questions intelligence failures
item.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye The presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Peter Obi, has mourned victims of the latest attacks in Plateau State, condemned the recurring killings in the state and questioned intelligence failures that have left communities vulnerable. In a statement posted on his X handle on Wednesday, Obi called for stronger security measures, thorough investigations and justice for the victims, saying the continued loss of lives showed the need for urgent action to protect Nigerians. “I am deeply saddened and troubled by reports that at least nine people were killed in the Zuwagal community, Mangu Local Government Area of Plateau State, in yet another assault on innocent Nigerians,” Obi said. He described the killings as part of a “deeply concerning pattern of recurring attacks, displacement and the destruction of communities throughout the country.” Citing OpenWatch security incident records, Obi said 261 deaths were reported across Nigeria between November 2 and 15, including 24 in Plateau during the first week and 15 in the second. He added that Plateau recorded further attacks on November 16. “These victims are not merely numbers. They were fathers, mothers, children and breadwinners whose lives were abruptly ended, leaving families and entire communities to mourn,” he said, extending his condolences to the bereaved families and the people of Plateau State. Obi questioned why communities continued to face threats without adequate protection and why intelligence reports were not leading to preventive action. He called on the government and security agencies to reinforce operations in vulnerable communities, investigate the attacks, establish reliable early-warning and rapid-response systems, support displaced families and ensure those responsible were brought to justice. “Every Nigerian life is valuable, regardless of ethnicity, religion or political affiliation. The right to life must never be subject to negotiation,” he said. “Nigeria must do more than mourn those who have died. We must protect those who are still living.” Vanguard reported that at least five people were killed in fresh attacks on communities in Mangu, Riyom and Barkin Ladi local government areas. The latest incident occurred at about 9pm on Sunday, November 15, when suspected terrorists attacked Zwagal community in Jipal District, Mangu, killing three people, while others were reported missing. Two other people were killed in separate attacks in Riyom and Barkin Ladi. The Berom Youth Moulders Association said Da Ishaku Pam Vwos, 79, was killed in Sho village, Barkin Ladi, and Dauda John Davou, 42, was killed in Sambak community, Riyom. The association also said attackers entered Jol community but met resistance from local vigilantes. item.title: Subsidy benefits went to intermediaries, not Nigerians — Uzodimma
item.description: By John Alechenu ABUJA — Imo State Governor, Hope Uzodimma, has said the benefits of Nigeria’s petroleum subsidy regime largely accrued to intermediaries in the oil sector rather than ordinary Nigerians it was designed to protect. Uzodimma stated this on Wednesday while delivering an address at the ongoing 13th World Public Relations Forum 2026 in Abuja. The forum was organised by the Global Alliance for Public Relations and Communication Management and hosted by the Nigerian Institute of Public Relations (NIPR). The governor said responsible governance required building public trust through community engagement, stakeholder relations and inclusive development. He described one of the greatest tests of leadership as taking difficult decisions that initially hurt the people but are expected to benefit them in the long run, while maintaining honest communication to secure public understanding and trust. He said: “I like to think about leadership, the experience I learned in leading Imo State as governor and keeping the trust. Especially when you want to accept a decision that will hurt people first before such decisions will help them. “It is even tougher when the administration is new and when the people are yet to see tangible results they can relate to.” Citing the removal of the petroleum subsidy as an example, Uzodimma said the policy was originally intended to ease the burden on ordinary Nigerians but that much of its benefits went to intermediaries in the petroleum sector. “The petroleum subsidy was meant to help ordinary Nigerians. But most of the benefits ended up with intermediaries in the sector,” he said. He defended President Bola Tinubu’s decision to remove the subsidy, describing it as necessary in the overall interest of the country. According to him, Nigerians across different sectors and segments of society had openly called for the removal of the subsidy before the policy was implemented. “Do not forget that before he did that, Nigerians across different sectors and segments had openly canvassed and demanded that it be removed,” he said. The governor further argued that the removal had increased the resources available to state governments and the Federal Capital Territory for infrastructure and socioeconomic development. He, however, acknowledged that the resulting price adjustments had created difficulties for many households, stressing that reforms were more likely to deliver their intended benefits when citizens understood the reasons behind them. Using an example from Imo State, Uzodimma explained how government interventions could benefit some groups while initially affecting the livelihoods of others. He said the introduction of modern buses operating at affordable fares along busy routes in Owerri would reduce transportation costs for workers, traders and students but could affect commercial drivers who might see the initiative as a threat to their businesses. item.title: Super Eagles move up to 29th in latest FIFA world rankings
item.description: The Nigerian Super Eagles have moved up one place to 29th in the latest FIFA men’s world rankings released on Wednesday. The improvement also sees the team climb to fifth position among African countries, overtaking Algeria, which dropped out of the continent’s top five. The Super Eagles’ latest progress comes after their two November fixtures against Tanzania in the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations qualifying campaign. Eric Chelle’s men began the international window with a 3-1 victory over the Taifa Stars at the Godswill Akpabio International Stadium in Uyo last Friday. However, Nigeria failed to maintain their winning run, settling for a goalless draw against the same opponents in Tuesday’s return fixture at the Amaan Stadium in Zanzibar. Morocco retained their position as Africa’s highest-ranked team, followed by Senegal, Egypt and Côte d’Ivoire in second, third and fourth places, respectively. On the global ranking, Spain maintained their position as the world’s number one team, while Argentina, France and England retained their places among the top five. item.description: The Nigeria Labour Congress (NLC) and the Trade Union Congress of Nigeria (TUC) have resolved their recent disagreement, following the recent banter over the N70,000 one-off six-month allowance approved by President Tinubu. The two labour centres announced the resolution of the dispute on Wednesday at a joint press conference held in Abuja. In a joint statement signed by NLC President, Joe Ajaero, and TUC President-General, Festus Osifo, the unions acknowledged that their disagreement had played out publicly but insisted that their shared history and responsibility to Nigerian workers must take precedence over leadership and institutional differences. Reaffirming their commitment to a united labour movement and the collective defence of workers’ rights, they described the disagreement as a family misunderstanding that had now been amicably settled through the intervention of former leaders of both organisations. While speaking on Channels Television’s The Morning Brief recently, Comrade Joe Ajero argued that the Union has the power to negotiate alone on labour matters based on the principle of most workers representatives of the International Labour Organization (ILO). “TUC can negotiate along with NLC, but NLC can negotiate alone based on the principle of most workers representatives of the ILO”, the NLC President noted. On his part, the TUC President, while also appearing as a guest on Channels Television’s The Morning Brief , described the N70,000 agreement by the NLC President as an aberration, saying that the TUC was not carried along in the negotiations. Osifo challenged Ajaero to produce the ILO regulation document that said either of the labour unions could negotiate on behalf of the other. “He should show me in the ILO Regulations where it says one party is going to negotiate without the other one being there or consulted. He should show me! He should show Nigerians! NLC determines how TUC participates”, Ajaero adding that the TUC does not submit its proposal to TUC. “It is the other way round,” he stated that the Ministry of Labour and other labour authorities will not engage with the Trade Union, as it acts alone on workers’ welfare negotiations. The trade congress leader, in his reply, said, “As I listened to Ajaero today, I was wondering if it is the same NLC that produced the likes of Adams Oshiomole, Hassan Sumonu, Ayuba Wabba and so on. “There is nowhere in ILO regulations that says a trade centre cannot negotiate for its members. item.title: ‘Fake Agency’ Case: Adeyemi in custody for his own safety, ICPC tells court
item.description: … as defendants plead not guilty, beg for bail By Ikechukwu Nnochiri ABUJA — The Independent Corrupt Practices and Other Related Offences Commission (ICPC) said on Wednesday that it kept the self-styled Director-General (DG) of the alleged “non-existent” Presidential Foreign Investment Promotion Council (PFIPC), Prince Adeniyi Adeyemi, in custody for his own safety. According to the Commission, many of those allegedly defrauded by the defendant, a number of whom have filed petitions against him, are capable of physically harming him on sight. It therefore prayed the High Court of the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), sitting at Maitama in Abuja, to reject an application that Adeyemi filed to be released on bail pending the determination of the criminal charge against him. “My lord, the defendant is facing allegations of obtaining by false pretence. “There are many petitions against him, and the people who lodged those petitions are after him. “There is this particular man from Ibadan whom he defrauded, which formed part of the counts in the charge. He has been seriously searching for him. “We believe that it will be in his own best interest to remain in custody for safekeeping,” the prosecution counsel, Mr. Sylvanus Tahir, SAN, added. The ICPC urged the court to also deny bail to four civil servants who are facing trial alongside the alleged fake PFIPC DG. The anti-corruption agency took the position after the defendants pleaded not guilty to a 36-count amended charge it entered against them. All the defendants, through their respective lawyers, begged the court to release them on bail pending the determination of the charge. They anchored their bail applications on the provisions of sections 35(4) and 36(5) of the 1999 Constitution, as amended, as well as sections 158 and 162 of the Administration of Criminal Justice Act (ACJA) 2015. The civil servants who were docked alongside Adeyemi on Wednesday are Aminu Abdullahi, Ogaba Harry, Florence Omameh and Patricia Akhigbe. All the defendants, including Adeyemi, pleaded ill health, even as they pledged to make themselves available for trial. However, the prosecution counsel urged the court to refuse their bail requests and order an accelerated hearing of the case. The ICPC specifically alleged that Adeyemi posed a flight risk, insisting he had enough funds at his disposal and the capacity to influence some of the proposed witnesses in the matter. Meanwhile, in urging the court to grant him bail on very liberal terms, Adeyemi, through his counsel, Mr. Ibrahim Angulu, SAN, told the court that, contrary to the prosecution’s claim, all his bank accounts had been frozen. “My lord, the accounts of the defendant were frozen, including those of his wives. They have all been frozen. So he does not have the means to escape or to influence the witnesses,” Adeyemi’s lawyer insisted. item.title: Nigeria still yearns for visionary leaders like Nnamdi Azikiwe – Abaribe
item.description: By Nwabueze Okonkwo ONITSHA – Senator Enyinnaya Abaribe representing Abia South Senator District, has praised the leadership philosophy of Nigeria’s first President, the late Dr Nnamdi Azikiwe, lamenting that the country is still struggling to find leaders capable of providing the kind of purposeful leadership championed by the late nationalist He stated that Azikiwe demonstrated exemplary leadership through his emphasis on education, social reorientation, freedom, infrastructural development and visionary thinking, which he used as instruments for shaping society and advancing national development. Senator Abaribe who made the remarks during the 14th edition of the Zik Lecture Series held under the theme, “Zik’s Vision for Renaissance: Lessons from Emerging Economies in Africa”, identified himself as a student of Zik’s leadership philosophy, noting that the late statesman represented a generation of leaders whose political influence was guided by clear principles and a strong commitment to societal transformation. According to Abaribe, “leadership, as demonstrated by Azikiwe, went beyond the acquisition of political power to include the effective use of available resources and opportunities to influence the direction of a people”. He expressed concern that several African countries, particularly Nigeria, had continued to search for leaders committed to the principles of purposeful governance long after Azikiwe’s departure. Highlighting some of the challenges confronting Nigeria, the lawmaker identified weaknesses in the education sector, the growing divide between moral and immoral values, uncontrolled exposure to social media and the breakdown of family structures as issues requiring urgent attention. He, however, expressed optimism that recognising and acknowledging these problems would constitute an important step towards finding lasting solutions. Abaribe explained that his intention was not necessarily to provide immediate solutions but to draw attention to the deep-rooted challenges confronting the country and the African continent. He urged Nigerians to reflect deeply on the situation and take deliberate steps towards breaking the cycle of societal problems. Earlier, the Vice-Chancellor of Nnamdi Azikiwe University, Prof. Okechukwu Bond Anyiehie, described the theme of the lecture as timely and relevant to the country’s quest for development. Anyaehie noted that universities should not be seen merely as institutions for awarding academic degrees but as centres for generating ideas capable of driving societal transformation. Addressing the graduating students, whom he fondly referred to as Great Zikites, the Vice-Chancellor urged them to carry forward the ideals of courage, intellectual excellence, scholarship and Pan-Africanism associated with the late Azikiwe. item.title: EU proposes new 45bn euro Ukraine loan
item.description: The European Union on Wednesday proposed member states give Ukraine an extra 45-billion-euro ($49 billion) loan to plug Kyiv’s 2027 budget shortfalls as Russia’s war drags on. The funding would go two-thirds of the way towards filling a 70-billion-euro black hole Kyiv is facing next year — with Brussels looking to incentivise other Ukraine backers to do the rest. “Five years since the start of this war of aggression, Europe stands united. We are as committed as ever to support Ukraine in war and in peace,” European Commission chief Ursula von der Leyen said. “We think this is the best way to give Ukraine a strong hand at the negotiation table, and Ukraine only needs to repay once Russia pays for the damage it has caused in Ukraine.” EU leaders will discuss the loan at a summit in Brussels next week in the hope of reaching a deal. The EU is currently paying out a 90-billion-loan to Kyiv that it hoped would see the country through to the end of next year. But as Russia has intensified its attacks it has become clear that those funds would not be enough. The new loan would follow the same format as the current one and be borrowed against headroom in the EU’s central budget. It would also be linked to Kyiv pressing on with reforms. While the aim is to forge agreement next week, the issue of the funding has now become wrapped up with broader fraught negotiations over the EU’s next central budget. Budget brawl German Chancellor Friedrich Merz has insisted that all of the EU must settle the financing and all 27 member states must be involved before a deal can be reached on the budget. That has rankled several of the EU’s least pro-Ukraine countries who want to be left out of backing the loan, such as Bulgaria, the Czech Republic, Hungary, and Slovakia. Last time round, Budapest, Bratislava and Prague managed to get themselves exempted from having to help cover the financing. Von der Leyen insisted the aim this time remains to get all countries on board. Beyond the bloc, Brussels is pushing other allies of Ukraine – such as Britain, Canada and Japan to fill in the rest of Kyiv’s needs next year. Similar pleas have previously fallen short. In a bid to incentivise them this time, Brussels says others could provide guarantees to help bolster the loan or use the interest on frozen Russian assets in the EU to cover their own financing. The proposal for a new loan means that the EU for now won’t try to look into the thorny issue of directly tapping over 200 billion euros of frozen Russian central bank assets held in the bloc to fund Ukraine. That plan was shot down in 2025 by Belgium — where the majority of the assets are held — and the position of its government has not shifted.
